page: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-96xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. The platform exposes 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz. Cache architecture consists of 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a unified 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8). System memory totals 3072.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, delivering an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The server includes a 100 Gbps baseline networking interface, contains zero integrated local storage, and includes no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show exceptional parallel execution and memory subsystem bandwidth. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 417,683.29 and a PassMark CPU score of 180,710.06, supported by strong cryptographic and extended instruction capabilities. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 1,148.36 GB/sec with 443.25 GB/sec write bandwidth, enabling top-tier database operations in PassMark (34,161.11) and 531.59 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 2,260.38 GB/sec and Clang compilation scores 66,244.0. In contrast, single-core CPU throughput registers in average ranges, and text-generation LLM inference remains constrained on pure CPU execution compared to prompt processing.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server maximizes density for large memory footprints, eliminating hypervisor overhead via its bare-metal configuration. Because local storage is absent, all persistent data depends on network-attached storage or remote services over the 100 Gbps fabric. The hardware profile is engineered primarily for in-memory databases such as Redis and SAP HANA, large-scale software compilation, real-time analytics, and enterprise data transformation workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-96xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The platform delivers 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated vCPUs clocked at up to 3.9 GHz, accompanied by 480 MB of L3 cache with AMX and AVX-512 vector support. System memory provides 3072.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM at 7 GHz, equating to 8.0 GB per vCPU, coupled with a 100 Gbps network interface. It features zero discrete GPUs and no onboard local storage. Performance benchmarks highlight top-tier throughput in multi-core computing (417,683.29 on stress-ng), Redis SET transactions (531.59 million ops/sec), and memory bandwidth surpassing 1,148 GB/sec on large uncached blocks. This hardware configuration is targeted for in-memory databases, large data transformation pipelines, distributed caching layers, and high-concurrency software build systems.
